topic: DSH Lark Bridge: Chat with DeepSeek Harness agents on Feishu/Lark

key_points: Native dsh plugin bridging DeepSeek Harness coding agents to Feishu/Lark group chats — one group = one isolated project folder
Persistent per-chat sessions, survive restarts; /new clears a session
File & image support (.attachments/<messageId>/ folder): 5 attachments/msg, images <=10MB, other files <=20MB, swept after 7 days
Zero-config: first launch auto-runs a QR registration wizard that creates the Feishu app for you — no portal setup
Long-lived WebSocket to Feishu → no public IP or callback URL needed
Slash commands: /help /new /where /models /whoami (local); owner-only /model /preset /allow /disallow (shared state)
Needs DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access because Feishu users can't click a local approval prompt; only trust env
Install: pnpm setup (builds+links+registers) or dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path; Windows uses junction not symlink
Scan QR in 30s, control local coding agent from phone/group/topic; stays responsive even if agent crashes
Feishu WebSocket long-connection — no public IP/domain/server/内网穿透; Node.js >= 22
Install: npx dsh-lark-bot@latest setup --profile dsh-lark, then dsh --profile dsh-lark
Existing app can skip QR: DSH_LARK_APP_ID=cli_xxx DSH_LARK_APP_SECRET=... DSH_LARK_TENANT=feishu dsh --profile dsh-lark
Streaming cards, multiple agents/roles, cross-session notification, in-chat model & key management, safety-net guardian
Upgrade via npx dsh-lark-bot@latest upgrade; AGPLv3 license; listed on dshfind/dshbase/dsh-plugin.org
npm i -g dsh-lark-channel && dsh-lark-channel start (or npx dsh-lark-channel@latest start)
Terminal prints QR; scan to create app/bind; then DM the bot or @it in group
First run pre-writes profile pnpm build strategy — auto-skips unapproved build scripts, no manual pnpm approve-builds needed
Not just a chatbot: can switch real workdir & model, run existing harness commands/tools (/status /ws /cd /model)
Q&A, plan review and tool approval cards surface in Feishu; button/text answers; per-chat/topic/workspace context isolation
Add multiple agents to one group; they hand off turns via @ mention with a round cap to stop infinite loops
npm latest 0.0.7; BSD-3-Clause
Multi-channel remote access for DeepSeek Harness — WeChat/QQ/Feishu/Telegram bots + PWA plus Cloudflare or self-built public tunnel
Feishu via WebSocket 2.0; Node.js >= 22.19/24
Access auth + PBKDF2 security gate; npm package @wenbin_wb/dsh-bridge
Positions itself as the broader remote-control suite (not Lark-only): LAN scan direct connect, phone/tablet PWA
High-reliability Feishu/Lark bridge for DeepSeek Harness — QR one-click auth, multi-mode agents

stats.fact: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness (DSH, 'Everything is a Plugin') is a TypeScript plugin-based AI agent harness built on Cordis, ~204K stars, homepage deepseek.com/harness
The official CLI/package is @deepseek-ai/dsh on npm (latest 0.1.1-rc.2), first published 2026-08-10
dsh's plugin ecosystem is distributed via npm; plugins like dsh-lark-channel and @wenbin_wb/dsh-bridge install globally and register into a dsh profile
Feishu/Lark Long Connection (WebSocket 2.0) lets bots receive messages without a public callback URL or public IP — the bridge connects out to Feishu over a persistent socket

Remote-agent approval UX: because Feishu/Lark users cannot click a local approval prompt, bridge plugins require the host to run with DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access (agent approval policy 'never') in a trusted environment

angles: Comparison of 4-5 dsh↔Feishu bridge plugins and which to choose (native plugin vs npx-channel vs multi-channel gateway)
Zero-public-IP setup: WebSocket long-connection means no tunnel/callback/server needed — a key selling point
Security & permission model: danger-full-access trade-off and mitigation (allow/disallow lists, trusted env)
Team workflow: one group = one project workspace, multiple agents in a group handing off turns via @
QR-based onboarding: first-run wizard that auto-creates the Feishu app → near-zero setup friction
Chat UX in Feishu vs terminal: slash commands, streaming cards, plan/approval cards, file/image attachment handling
